description: I am MD. Shihab Ahmed. I study Dhaka land subsidence with Sentinel-1 InSAR. My pilot showed dense-urban Dhaka has a stable radar signal for tracking change (urban-proxy mean coherence 0.587; 78% of pixels ≥ 0.4). For Dancing with the SARs, I am building Dhaka Is Sinking, an interactive app using NISAR radar data to map surface change. I work solo but welcome one or two teammates, especially in coding or design.
summary: Project NISARWatch asks one question: can radar see Dhaka clearly enough to track the ground beneath it? Dhaka depends on groundwater while construction keeps adding load, so the ground may be sinking — but before anyone can measure how fast, the radar signal itself must be proven reliable. We processed a 12-day Sentinel-1 pair (13–25 December 2023) over Motijheel and Old Dhaka and found the dense-urban signal is stable: urban-proxy mean coherence 0.587, with 78% of urban pixels at or above 0.4. The vegetated fringe (Purbachal, 0.379, 42%) is too weak for this method and is gated out. We also catalogued 48 provisional NISAR L2 GUNW granules over Dhaka and built a transparent Watch Index (Motijheel 8.34 of 9) that ranks where monitoring should start. The interactive app presents the map, the comparison, the NISAR catalogue and the index in one place. No subsidence rate is claimed — the pilot measured signal, not sinking; the full 2017–2025 time series is the next step.
details:
Problem: Dhaka depends almost entirely on groundwater, while construction keeps adding load on top of the city. Together, these pressures create a risk that the ground sinks, threatening buildings and roads. But before anyone can measure how fast the ground is moving, one question must be answered first: can radar see this dense city clearly enough to track change at all?

What we did: we ran an original Sentinel-1 coherence pilot — four IW SLC scenes (19 November – 25 December 2023) processed in ESA SNAP 14 with snaphu 2.0.5, a 10x3 coherence window, and an urban proxy from the top 25% of backscatter. Over Motijheel and Old Dhaka, the urban-proxy mean coherence is 0.587 (median 0.619), and 78% of urban-proxy pixels score 0.4 or higher — so the signal is stable enough to attempt a full time-series. Over the vegetated fringe (Purbachal / Jalsiri) the same method gives only 0.379 and 42%, so that area is gated as "cannot be assessed" by PSI and needs SBAS/DS instead. We also catalogued 48 provisional NISAR L2 GUNW granules over Dhaka (18 June – 18 October 2026; tracks 69_A_013, 69_A_014, 91_D_076, 91_D_077, 19_D_076; 45 SH and 3 SV), and documented three ARIA Sentinel-1 GUNW records covering 2015–2022.

What the app shows: a single interactive observatory — a Dhaka study-area map, the urban-vs-fringe coherence comparison, an interferogram pair explorer, the NISAR granule catalogue, an interactive Watch Index (S(a) = 3xT(a) + G(a) + L(a); Motijheel scores 8.34 of 9), SAR geometry and C-band versus L-band comparison, and evidence cards with full provenance for every number. A guided audit path walks the reader through each claim, and a Phase 2 roadmap shows what comes next.

What we did not claim: the pilot measured signal stability, not how much the ground sank. No subsidence rate in mm/year is reported anywhere, because the pilot did not measure displacement. The unwrapped phase is not shown as displacement, the NISAR granules are labelled provisional, and the Watch Index is a monitoring priority, not a geological measurement.

Tools: HTML, CSS and JavaScript with Leaflet.js for the dashboard; ESA SNAP 14, snaphu 2.0.5 and Python for processing and statistics; NASA Earthdata Search and ASF Search for data discovery; ARIA-tools, MintPy and ISCE3 for the planned Phase 2 time-series work.

Who it helps: city planners (RAJUK), researchers, and anyone who needs to know where the ground is most at risk before buildings and roads are damaged — not after. The project is creative because it turns an honest "can we even measure this?" test into a working public tool: one place, one number, one decision, with the limits stated as clearly as the results.

Project Github repository: https://github.com/shihab-collab/dhaka-sar-watch
